I believe the commonly accepted use of “syncing” in the context of music devices is to keep playlists or libraries in the same state, in two or more places.

For example, if I have a playlist on my computer with songs A, B, and C, and I sync the playlist to my USB device, I expect the 3 songs to be copied over. If I delete song B from the playlist on my computer and sync again, I expect my USB device to now only contain songs A and C.

foobar’s copy only sends files to the target folder without caring about existing files, so you’ll still have to do some manual pruning with a file manager if you edit playlists often.

digital files outside of bullshit DRM like iTunes

As an aside, I use iTunes (the software) exclusively with DRM-free tracks purchased from DRM-free stores like Bandcamp. iTunes (the store/service) is a different matter. Syncing has nothing to do with DRM and is just about convenience over manual file management.

EDIT: I delete itunes from my laptop (yeah, it's a fucking mac) almost on a daily basis. It's like herpes. Every time it reinstalls, it re-routes my shortcut F keys to itunes so they don't work with VLC until it's both running and itunes is deleted.

I've tried to get help with a script that will run twice a day to delete itunes, but people always either respond with "why would you want to get rid of itunes, it's awesome lol" or mention a type of code with no indication of what to do with it.

You don’t need to delete iTunes to have VLC work with your media keys; VLC just needs to be running. In fact if both VLC and iTunes are running, VLC takes precedence as long as iTunes is not the active application (i.e. VLC is active or both are inactive).

iTunes also doesn’t automatically reinstall itself. You might have the App Store setup to automatically install app updates, and it’s detecting iTunes as requiring an update because it’s missing. Just uncheck “Install app updates” and “Install OS X updates” in System Preferences > App Store — you can leave the other options checked.
